item.title: Three schoolgirls in Kinsale pulled up a pea plant covered in warts (2016)
item.description:
📝 The scoreboard Irish science noticed first. They were 16 and 17, and they had started at 14, on a plant most gardeners would have thrown away. Three teenagers were told a biological door was closed, checked the literature, found that nobody had pushed on it with 13,000 seeds and three years of patience, and pushed.
🔗 Read more: https://scienceblog.com/b-three-schoolgirls-in-kinsale-pulled-up-a-pea-plant-covered-in-warts-and-instead-of-binning-it-spent-three-years-testing-13000-seeds-in-a-spare-bedroom-the-bacteria-living-in-those-warts-made-barley/

item.title: Japan halves speed limit to 30km/h on all narrow city streets
item.description:
📝 Narrow roads with no pavements are a common sight in crowded Japanese cities, with data indicating that children and older people are at particular risk of being involved in serious accidents. Photograph: imagenavi/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenNarrow roads with no pavements are a common sight in crowded Japanese cities, with data indicating that children and older people are at particular risk of being involved in serious accidents. Narrow roads with no centre lines or pavements are a common sight in crowded Japanese cities, with data indicating that children and older people are at particular risk of being involved in a fatal or serious accident.
🔗 Read more: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/02/japan-new-speed-limit-30kmh-narrow-city-streets
